*Amphisbaena alba*  LINNAEUS, 1758 is the species from the amphisbaenidae family with the biggest geographic distribution, encompassing all of South America. This species has a diversified diet that includes plants and small invertebrates. The species from the amphisbaenidae family have fossorial habits and spend most of their time burried, wich hinders studies on their ecology. This 3D model is a part of a study that aims to describe the brain of Amphisbaena alba and to understand more about this family’s anatomy, evolution, physiology and ecology.

Dissection: Bianca Rossi

The paiche, pirarucu, or arapaima is one of the largest freshwater fish in the world, growing to over 3 meters in length and weighing up to 250 kg.

In Brazil, it is known as “pirarucu,” a name that comes from the Tupi language and means “red fish.”

This fish inhabits the rivers of the Amazon rainforest basin and is primarily carnivorous, feeding on smaller fish, although it may also consume plant matter and crustaceans.

They are perfectly adapted to habitats with low oxygen concentrations, especially during the dry season. Its main threat is overfishing.

name: カバトゲウミギク / Spondylus butleri
description:
殻は類円形で大型になり、右殻で岩礁などに固着して生活する。橙色、赤紫色などの個体がある。左右の殻の色違いは非常に珍しい。紀伊半島以南、インド・西太平洋に分布し、水深5～20ｍの岩礁に生息。

The shell is subcircular and grows to a large size; the right valve attaches to rocky reefs and other substrates. Some individuals are orange or reddish-purple in color. It is extremely rare for the left and right valves to differ in color. This species is found south of the Kii Peninsula, as well as in the Indian and Western Pacific Oceans, inhabiting rocky reefs at depths of 5 to 20 meters.
